title: Idioms & phrasal verbs
description: 55 original questions: the earlier 40 plus 15 Moderate–Hard items. Select Moderate–Hard for close alternatives and complete meaning checks. This is a reviewed training target, not an independently calibrated exam rating.

collocations: rule out an explanation / rule it out
vocabularyCandidates.readingExample: The missing receipt did not rule out a valid payment, so the auditor checked the transaction log.

vocabularyCandidates.meaning: perform or complete a task or instruction
collocations: carry out an audit / carry the checks out
vocabularyCandidates.readingExample: The independent team will carry out the audit before the funds are released.

collocations: look into a complaint / look into it
vocabularyCandidates.readingExample: The bank agreed to look into the unexplained charge and examine the payment records.

vocabularyCandidates.meaning: at risk or dependent on the outcome
collocations: savings at stake / public confidence at stake
vocabularyCandidates.readingExample: With public confidence at stake, the bank published a clear account of the error.

vocabularyCandidates.meaning: something that distracts attention from the relevant question or issue
collocations: a red herring in the debate / introduce a red herring
vocabularyCandidates.readingExample: The accurate growth figure became a red herring when it diverted attention from the unresolved liquidity problem.

vocabularyCandidates.meaning: according to the apparent meaning or appearance, without further examination
collocations: take a claim at face value / accept an assurance at face value
vocabularyCandidates.readingExample: The reviewer did not accept the assurance at face value and asked for independent evidence.

vocabularyCandidates.meaning: tolerate or endure an unpleasant situation or behaviour
collocations: put up with delays / put up with them
vocabularyCandidates.readingExample: Borrowers would no longer put up with unexplained charges and asked for a written account.

questions.prompt: The bank will ___ the complaint by examining the transaction records.
questions.instructions: Choose the single best answer using the complete context.

explanation.relationship: Context and construction: keep the intended action and direction
explanation.clue: Examining the records is investigation.
explanation.rule: Look into a complaint means investigate it.
explanation.model: The bank will look into the complaint by examining the transaction records.

rejects.reason: Look after means care for; the task here is investigation.
Look up to means admire, not investigate a complaint.
Look down on means regard with contempt, not investigate.
Look out for means watch for something, not investigate this existing complaint.

questions.prompt: The audit team has not yet begun the work; it must ___ the checks specified in the approved procedure.
questions.instructions: Choose the single best answer using the complete context.

explanation.relationship: Context and construction: keep the intended action and direction
explanation.clue: Specified checks are to be performed.
explanation.rule: Carry out a check means perform it.
explanation.model: The audit team has not yet begun the work; it must carry out the checks specified in the approved procedure.

rejects.reason: Carry off can mean succeed in doing something difficult; it is not the ordinary perform-the-checks construction here.
Carry over means transfer or postpone to a later period.
Carry on with means continue; this instruction specifies performing the checks, without a prior activity to continue.
Carry away means remove or transport, not perform checks.

questions.prompt: The panel decided to ___ the hearing until Friday, rather than cancel it.
questions.instructions: Choose the single best answer using the complete context.

explanation.relationship: Context and construction: keep the intended action and direction
explanation.clue: Until Friday and rather than cancel distinguish postponement from cancellation.
explanation.rule: Put off a hearing means postpone it.
explanation.model: The panel decided to put off the hearing until Friday, rather than cancel it.

rejects.reason: Call off cancels the event, explicitly excluded here.
Rule out excludes a possibility; it does not reschedule a hearing.
Bring forward moves an event earlier, contrary to postponement until Friday.
Take over means assume control, not postpone.

questions.prompt: After the project was abandoned permanently, the bank decided to ___ the launch altogether.

rejects.reason: Put off merely postpones; abandoned permanently and altogether require cancellation.
Carry out performs the launch, opposite to abandoning it.
Bring about causes an event, rather than cancels it.
Look into investigates, rather than cancels.

questions.prompt: The evidence did not ___ the possibility of a clerical error; investigators still had to check it.

explanation.relationship: Context and construction: keep the intended action and direction
explanation.clue: The possibility remains to be checked.
explanation.rule: Not rule out means not exclude; it does not mean the possibility has been proved.

rejects.reason: Evidence does not mean cause a clerical error in this sentence.
A possibility is not an activity to perform.
Put up with means tolerate, not exclude a possibility.
Look after means care for, not eliminate an explanation.

questions.prompt: The panel postponed a final judgement until independent checks were complete; it did not conceal a known defect. It chose to ___ rather than ___.

explanation.relationship: paired idioms: contrast, relevance and negation
explanation.clue: The first gap is temporary suspension of a verdict for a stated evidential reason; the second is deliberate concealment.
explanation.rule: Do not reject an idiom just because it is negative. Map both expressions to the two distinct actions.
explanation.model: The panel chose to reserve judgement rather than sweep the issue under the carpet.

rejects.option: sit on the fence / reserve judgement
rejects.reason: Sit on the fence can suggest avoiding a decision, but the second phrase would contrast waiting with waiting, not with concealing the defect.

rejects.option: sweep the issue under the carpet / reserve judgement
rejects.reason: This reverses the supplied contrast by making concealment the panel’s chosen action.

rejects.option: jump to conclusions / keep an open mind
rejects.reason: Jump to conclusions is a premature judgement, contrary to waiting for independent checks.

rejects.option: take the claim at face value / hold off on a verdict
rejects.reason: Taking at face value accepts the claim without the scrutiny for which the panel is waiting.

difficultyReview.nearestAlternative: sit on the fence / reserve judgement
difficultyReview.whyNot: Sit on the fence can suggest avoiding a decision, but the second phrase would contrast waiting with waiting, not with concealing the defect.
